title: Authentication
description: In this guide, we'll look at how authentication works. Protocol offers two ways to authenticate your API requests: Basic authentication and OAuth2 with a token.
content: authentication you'll need to authenticate your requests to access any of the endpoints in the protocol api. in this guide, we'll look at how authentication works. protocol offers two ways to authenticate your api requests: basic authentication and oauth2 with a token — oauth2 is the recommended way. classname: 'lead' basic authentication with basic authentication, you use your username and password to authenticate your http requests. unless you have a very good reason, you probably shouldn't use basic auth. here's how to authenticate using curl: please don't commit your protocol password to github! oauth2 with bearer token the recommended way to authenticate with the protocol api is by using oauth2. when establishing a connection using oauth2, you will need your access token — you will find it in the protocol dashboard under api settings. here's how to add the token to the request header using curl: always keep your token safe and reset it if you suspect it has been compromised. using an sdk if you use one of our official sdks, you won't have to worry about any of the above — fetch your access token from the protocol dashboard under api settings, and the client library will take care of the rest. all the client libraries use oauth2 behind the scenes. ::button url: '/sdks', variant: 'text' check out our list of first-party sdks ::icon arrow-right ::

title: Pagination
description: In this guide, we will look at how to work with paginated responses when querying the Protocol API
content: pagination in this guide, we will look at how to work with paginated responses when querying the protocol api. by default, all responses limit results to ten. however, you can go as high as 100 by adding a parameter to your requests. if you are using one of the official protocol api client libraries, you don't need to worry about pagination, as it's all being taken care of behind the scenes. classname: 'lead' when an api response returns a list of objects, no matter the amount, pagination is supported. in paginated responses, objects are nested in a attribute and have a attribute that indicates whether you have reached the end of the last page. you can use the and query parameters to browse pages. example using cursors ::row ::col in this example, we request the page that starts after the conversation with id . as a result, we get a list of three conversations and can tell by the attribute that we have reached the end of the resultset. ::properties ::property name: 'startingafter', type: 'string' the last id on the page you're currently on when you want to fetch the next page. ::property name: 'endingbefore', type: 'string' the first id on the page you're currently on when you want to fetch the previous page. ::property name: 'limit', type: 'integer' limit the number of items returned. :: ::col ::

title: Errors
description: In this guide, we will talk about what happens when something goes wrong while you work with the API.
content: errors in this guide, we will talk about what happens when something goes wrong while you work with the api. mistakes happen, and mostly they will be yours, not ours. let's look at some status codes and error types you might encounter. classname: 'lead' you can tell if your request was successful by checking the status code when receiving an api response. if a response comes back unsuccessful, you can use the error type and error message to figure out what has gone wrong and do some rudimentary debugging before contacting support. ::callout before reaching out to support with an error, please be aware that 99% of all reported errors are, in fact, user errors. therefore, please carefully check your code before contacting protocol support. :: error types ::row ::col whenever a request is unsuccessful, the protocol api will return an error response with an error type and message. you can use this information to understand better what has gone wrong and how to fix it. most of the error messages are pretty helpful and actionable. here is a list of the two error types supported by the protocol api — use these to understand what you have done wrong. ::properties ::property name: 'apierror' this means that we made an error, which is highly speculative and unlikely. ::property name: 'invalidrequest' this means that you made an error, which is much more likely. :: ::col ::

title: MediaServer Overview
description: Comprehensive overview of NoMercy MediaServer component.
content: what is mediaserver? mediaserver is a core component of nomercy that handles media file storage, organization, and streaming. it provides efficient management of your entertainment content library with powerful indexing and search capabilities. key features media organization - automatic cataloging: automatically detect and categorize media files - smart tagging: intelligent tagging system for content discovery - folder structure: flexible organization supporting complex folder hierarchies - multi-format support: support for various video, audio, and image formats streaming capabilities - direct streaming: stream media directly to supported devices - format transcoding: automatic transcoding for optimal playback quality - adaptive bitrate: intelligent bitrate adjustment for different connection speeds - subtitle support: automatic subtitle detection and management performance & reliability - efficient indexing: fast indexing for quick content discovery - caching system: intelligent caching for improved performance - backup support: built-in backup and recovery mechanisms - monitoring: real-time monitoring of media library health supported media formats video formats - mp4, mkv, avi, mov, flv, webm, and more audio formats - mp3, flac, aac, ogg, wav, and more image formats - jpg, png, webp, gif, and more components mediaserver consists of several components: 1. indexer: scans and catalogs media files 2. database: stores metadata and configuration 3. streamer: handles media playback and delivery 4. monitor: tracks system health and performance getting started with mediaserver to get started with mediaserver: 1. configure mediaserver - set up paths and settings 2. add media folders to your library 3. let the indexer scan and organize your content 4. start streaming and enjoying your media next steps - configuration guide - detailed setup instructions - nomercy getting started - return to main guide - installation guide - complete installation reference

description: Common music player issues — no audio, crossfade not firing, lyrics out of sync, backend errors, and diagnostics.
content: troubleshooting does nothing symptom: call appears to succeed but no audible transition occurs. causes and fixes: 1. selected — the default backend uses a loop for crossfade ~50 fps. it is less accurate than . crossfade is functional but may be imperceptible on short durations. switch with for sample-accurate fades. 2. duration too short — the default is 5 seconds. if your track is shorter than the fade duration, the crossfade completes instantly. reduce in . 3. already transitioning — returns . wait for the event before starting another. 4. fired first — if track end and your manual call overlap, the plugin may have already advanced. use and in options instead of calling manually from . --- lyrics are not displayed symptom: is registered but no lyrics appear. causes and fixes: 1. no on the track — calls which falls back to . if neither is set, no fetch occurs. check your . 2. not registered — if you have not called , the plugin uses directly. this still works if the url is correct. 3. unsupported file extension — parser selection is by url extension. and are built-in. custom formats need . 4. cors blocked — the fetch must succeed from the browser. add headers on the lyric host or proxy through your own server. 5. event not fired — listen to . if it never fires, check the network tab for a failed fetch on the lyrics url. --- lyrics are out of sync symptom: lyrics display at the wrong time. causes and fixes: 1. lrc timestamp format — verify your file uses format. non-standard formats e.g. seconds-only will not parse correctly. 2. seek position not updating lyrics — if the user seeks, re-scans from the cue list. this is automatic. if it is not working, ensure you are listening to not polling . 3. clock drift with — the uses which is sample-accurate but may diverge from after long sessions. this is expected. use not for any sync you build. --- throws symptom: throws an error. causes and fixes: 1. safari and ios — requires a user gesture on ios. call only inside a click or touch handler. 2. context suspended — the may be suspended after a page visibility change. listen to and call on page show. 3. already using the requested backend — not an error, but verify with before switching. --- --- phase stuck in symptom: returns indefinitely. causes and fixes: 1. source url returns a non-media content-type — hls streams must return . mp3/flac must return an audio content-type. a redirect to a login page returns , which hangs the parser. 2. auth token expired and is not set — a 401 with no refresh config produces a stale request. provide in your setup config. 3. hls manifest parse error — enable debug logging to capture the raw error. --- debug logging enable verbose output: with , the player logs every event, state title: FAQ
description: Frequently asked questions about the NoMercy Music Player — setup, crossfade, lyrics, backends, and TypeScript.
content: faq what is the difference between and ? is the concrete class. is the interface you should use for consumer-held references props, context, dependency injection. this prevents consumers from depending on the concrete constructor and keeps the type boundary clean. --- how many player instances can i have? as many as you need. each call with a unique id creates an independent instance. they share no state and each has its own audio backend, queue, and plugin set. a typical app has one global instance. a multi-room app might have one per room. --- does the player work server-side ssr/node? no. the player requires browser apis: , , , . it will throw on import in a node environment. in ssr frameworks next.js, nuxt, import and initialize only in browser-side code. --- why does autoplay block in the browser? browsers require a user gesture before allowing audio playback. common patterns: - call inside a or event handler. - on page load, set up the player and queue, but defer until the first interaction. the event fires when setup is complete. you can queue tracks there, but do not call from unless you know a user gesture has already occurred. --- what formats are supported? title: Architecture
description: The five-layer model that separates generic player infrastructure from your application code. How kit, libraries, and plugins relate to each other.
content: architecture the player sdk is built on a strict five-layer model. every piece of code has a designated layer, and no layer may reach "down" into a layer below it or "up" into a layer above it without going through a defined port. what each layer knows | layer | package | knows about | |-------|---------|-------------| | 1. backend | , , etc. | browser media apis only | | 2. kit | | generic contracts — nothing video- or music-specific | | 3. per-library | , | domain types , and domain methods | | 4. built-in plugin | plugins shipped inside packages | generic behavior ui, eq, autoadvance. no server endpoints. | | 5. consumer plugin | your app code | everything — server endpoints, signalr, auth tokens, business rules | --- why this matters the boundary between layer 4 and layer 5 is the enforcement point. anything nomercy-specific lives at layer 5. built-in plugins layer 4 must work for any consumer, with any backend, without any knowledge of the nomercy infrastructure. the practical consequence: when you add a built-in plugin from the package, it does not import from your app. when you write a consumer plugin, it can import from anywhere, but it should not modify kit internals. --- adapter ports layer 2 kit exposes 28 named adapter ports. each port has a typed interface and a default implementation. you replace a port only when you need different behavior — for example, swapping for , or replacing the browser network monitor with a capacitor native adapter. the video and music library layers each add 4 additional ports video: backend, chapter source, thumbnail source, subtitle style store; music: audio backend, playlist generator, scrobbler, lyric source, similarity engine, now-playing art. see kit — adapters for the full port catalog. --- plugin layering in practice a typical app setup: layer-5 plugins can listen to events from layer-4 plugins using the typed class-form: --- three-package layout | npm package | layer | consumers | |-------------|-------|-----------| | | 2 kit + 4 built-in plugins | library authors, advanced consumers writing plugins directly against the kit | | | 3 + 4 | anyone building a video player | | | 3 + 4 | anyone building a music player | both library packages re-export everything from the kit, so consumers of the video or music player do not need to install the kit separately unless they are writing kit-level plugins. --- container class system boundary state classes on the player container element are applied by the kit's container-class-emit mixin — , , , , etc. these are kit-level, present regardless of which ui plugin is active. the ui overlay controls bar, seek bar, menus, spinner is 's domain. it reads the kit's state classes and adds its own dom into the container. never modifies state classes — it only reads them. this boundary is intentional: a consumer can build a completely custom ui plugin that responds to the same state classes without touching . the state source kit and the ui renderer plugin are decoupled. the exact class inventory and which mixin owns each class is tracked by the player-architect spine. pending spine's confirmation, assume: , , , , , , , are kit-owned. , , are -owned.

title: ABR and Bandwidth
description: bandwidth(), bandwidthEstimator(), canPlay(), and CanPlayResult — throughput estimation and device capability probing.
content: abr and bandwidth three methods that expose throughput estimation and decode-capability probing. bandwidthestimator read or replace the bandwidth estimator function. reading returns the currently wired estimator or if none is set. writing installs a custom estimator. the active stream source calls the function on every abr level decision. install your own estimator when you have out-of-band signal signalr quality report, server-sent bitrate hint that is more accurate than the default download-speed measurement. the estimator is called synchronously on the abr decision path — keep it fast. --- canplay probes whether the browser can decode a specific media profile smoothly. delegates to the platform adapter's bridge, which wraps the standard api. --- canplayresult means the codec is not supported — do not select this quality level. means the level is playable but the browser may drop frames under load — use as a last resort only. is typically seen on mobile devices with high-bitrate streams that the cpu decodes in software rather than through the hardware decoder pipeline. it is informational — takes precedence for quality selection. --- using canplay for quality filtering before rendering a quality picker, filter out levels the browser cannot handle: for hls streams, the video player's hdr-aware abr logic does this filtering automatically — it uses internally to exclude hdr levels on sdr displays. calling manually is only needed when building a custom quality ui that must pre-filter the level list. --- see also - media tracks — and - player state — for the abr/manual mode flag - metrics — in - platform — the platform port

title: Troubleshooting
description: Common setup and runtime problems with the NoMercy Player SDK. Symptoms, causes, and fixes — verified against kit source.
content: troubleshooting every entry below is verified against the kit source. if the symptom you're hitting isn't here, file an issue with a minimal reproduction. player never reaches symptom: hangs indefinitely. the event never fires. causes and fixes: 1. a plugin's returned a promise that never resolves. awaits all promises capped by , default 10 seconds before emitting . audit each registered plugin for async work without timeouts. 2. the container element doesn't exist in the dom at . the kit doesn't wait for the element to appear. ensure returns a non-null element before calling . 3. a plugin's rejected. check the console for events. the failed plugin is disabled; still fires for the remaining plugins. if you see no and no , the promise is stuck see 1. 4. you're inspecting the wrong instance. returns the same instance on every call with the same id. if two parts of your code call setup on different ids, they're different players. --- dev mode — hls manifest fails to load symptom: locally served files fail when opening the html directly via . cause: browser security policy blocks cross-origin requests from origins. hls segment fetches from any other origin including are blocked. fix: serve over : or use vite / webpack dev server / any local http server. --- framework ssr — player crashes during server-side render symptom: build or render crashes with or during ssr next.js, nuxt, sveltekit, astro. cause: the player depends on browser apis , , , . these don't exist in a node server environment. fix: lazy-load the player on the client only. next.js react: nuxt / vue: astro: use so the component never renders on the server. pick the directive that matches the component's framework: sveltekit: guard with from , or use which only fires client-side. --- two players on the same page share state symptom: two players appear to share state — controlling one affects the other. cause: and are factories backed by an internal registry. calls with the same return the same instance. two components using the same id are pointing at the same player. fix: use unique ids per instance: for a single-player app, picking a static id is fine. for multi-player uis pip, watch parties, tile grids, generate a stable id per slot. --- volume resets every page load symptom: the player ignores the user's saved volume preference. cause: the kit doesn't auto-persist volume. the default adapter persists arbitrary keys; reading volume from it on setup is the consumer's job. fix: read on , write on every event. volume is on the 0–100 scale. or use the kit's adapter pre-scoped per player id instead of raw . --- thrown by music player method symptom: calling on a music player throws with code . cause: audio backends don't have subtitle tracks. is on the shared player surface but is intentionally not implemented on . fix: catch the error by type. import from the kit: or — simpler — only call on video players. --- , , or throws on symptom: adding these music-player plugins, then fires with a . still fires for the remaining plugins. cause: all three are stubbed in and intentionally throw . full implementations are planned for . fix: don't register them yet. track progress in versioning. --- hls auth — segments return 401 after a delay symptom: hls manifest loads, playback starts, then segment requests start returning 401 after some time. or every segment 401s from the first request. cause token expiry: is a static string. the kit injects whatever value you passed at setup. if the token expires between manifest load and segment fetch, the injected value is stale. cause no refresh: isn't configured. the kit retries a 401 exactly once if a refresh function is provided; without it, the request fails immediately. fix: pass as a factory and provide a refresh function: the factory is called on every authenticated request — the player always sees the current token. on a 401, is called once and the request retries automatically. a 403 propagates and is never retried — that's an access-policy problem on the server, not an auth-token problem. --- inline of the kit fails — symptom: a consumer or a custom plugin imports from and the resolver can't find it. cause: the kit is the foundation under both and but isn't a transitive runtime dependency a consumer would see. if you're writing a plugin or adapter against the kit directly, you need to install the kit alongside. fix: if you only use the video or music package's surface no custom plugins, you don't need this — the per-library package re-exports what you need. --- container element class never updates symptom: the container should gain / etc. but the classes are missing. cause: state classes live on the element passed as to . if you re-mount the player into a fresh dom node e.g. ssr hydration replacing the host element, the kit's reference is to the old node. fix: don't re-create the container after setup. if you have to hmr, spa navigation, the player first and again on the new node. state classes are owned by the kit itself, not by — you get them even on a raw html container with no ui plugin installed. --- custom plugin's never fires symptom: a plugin declares with recovery actions but nothing happens when it throws. cause: is a declarative map — . the kit consults it when the plugin throws via . if your plugin throws directly with or emits via , the recovery map is bypassed. fix: always raise plugin errors through the base class helper: see plugin standard §1.8 for the full error escalation contract. --- plugin runs twice / plugin event listeners double up symptom: event handlers in a plugin's fire twice for every event. cause: most commonly, is being called manually in addition to the player calling it. don't invoke yourself — triggers the lifecycle. second cause: two different classes share the same . the kit allows this for replacement subclass with same id replaces the original but if both are added independently, both register and both listen. fix: ensure each plugin id is unique. use ids for third-party plugins , to avoid collisions with kit-shipped plugins. --- reporting a bug if the symptom isn't here, file an issue with: - kit version from - player package + version - browser + version - minimal html/js reproduction a public codesandbox / stackblitz link is ideal - console output with enabled

title: FAQ
description: Frequently asked questions about the NoMercy Player SDK.
content: faq can i use both the video player and music player on the same page? yes. each player instance is isolated by its id. the video player and music player share no global state beyond the internal instance registry. they do not interfere. you can have both playing at the same time subject to browser audio policy. if you need one to pause when the other plays, wire that coordination yourself in a consumer plugin or in your app code. --- how do i write my own subtitle renderer? replace the built-in vtt text rendering with your own plugin that implements the same interface. register your plugin with . for ass/ssa subtitles with full typesetting, add — it loads dynamically and handles its own rendering. do not combine and a custom renderer for the same subtitle track. see video — subtitle overlay for the full api. --- does the player handle 401 / 403 differently? yes. the auth pipeline treats them differently by design: - 401 — token expired. is called once, the new token is applied, and the request is retried. if refresh fails, an event fires and the request errors. - 403 — access denied. the error propagates immediately. is never called for 403s. the server has denied access even with valid credentials. never lump 401 and 403 in the same catch block. a 403 may signal an entitlement problem that no amount of token refreshing will fix. --- how do i add auto-advance play next track when the current one ends? add — it is shipped with both library packages: the plugin listens to the event and calls . when crossfade is enabled on the music player, it triggers instead. --- how do i pause all players at once? there is no global play/pause. you control each instance by id: if you need coordinated playback across multiple players group listening, use — planned for v2.1. --- can i use the player with typescript strict mode? yes. the packages ship full typescript types. all public methods are typed. the generic parameter or threads your playlist item type through , , , and events — no casts required. --- how do i render the player without the built-in ui? do not add . the player itself renders nothing — all chrome is opt-in through plugins. build your own controls using the event api: --- how do i restrict hls quality to avoid high bitrate on slow networks? is not related to quality. quality selection lives in the video player's hls adapter. set a maximum level via the config: to hard-cap to a specific quality level index at runtime: hdr-aware abr is automatic — on sdr displays, the player filters out hdr levels from the abr selection pool. no configuration needed. see video — hls for the full quality api. --- how do i listen to events from a plugin i did not write? import the plugin class and use the typed class-form: if you do not want to import the class, use the string form with the auto-namespaced event name: --- is the player compatible with capacitor, tauri, or electron? yes, via the platform adapter system. override individual sub-ports without rebuilding the entire bundle: the player's core logic only calls the interfaces — it does not import capacitor or tauri directly. --- where do i report bugs? - nomercy-video-player: github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-video-player/issues - nomercy-music-player: github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-music-player/issues - nomercy-player-core: github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-player-kit/issues

title: Auth & Fetch
description: The authFetch wrapper, bearer token injection, 401 vs 403 handling, and retry policy.
content: auth & fetch the player's pipeline handles all network requests made by the player and its built-in plugins. bearer tokens are injected automatically, 401 responses trigger a single refresh attempt, and 403 responses propagate immediately. configuration all fields are optional. without , requests are unauthenticated. --- auth config reference token or factory. a factory is called on every authenticated request — use a factory when the token can expire. a static string is applied as-is. the token is injected as . called once when a request returns 401. must return a new valid token. the failed request is retried exactly once with the new token. if refresh fails, fires and the error propagates to the caller. custom request signer — called after the bearer token is applied. use for hmac, api key rotation, or any custom signing scheme. static headers appended to every authenticated request. --- 401 vs 403 handling | response | behavior | |---------|---------| | 401 | called once → request retried. if refresh fails → event + error propagates. | | 403 | error propagates immediately. is never called for 403. | do not lump 401 and 403 together in your error handling. a 403 is an access policy decision — retrying with a refreshed token will not help. check the server's entitlement configuration instead. auth events: --- retry policy the default retry policy retries failed network requests 3 times with exponential backoff. configure or replace it via the adapter: auth refresh retries are separate from the general retry policy — is called exactly once, not retried. --- inside plugins: plugins should use instead of the global . this applies the player's auth config, respects the retry policy, and properly types the response: if you need the raw object before it is dispatched for example, to add a signature, use in the auth config rather than building it manually in the plugin. --- updating auth at runtime replace auth config after setup — for example, when a long-lived token is refreshed by an external mechanism: this merges the provided partial config with the existing auth config. only the fields you provide are updated.
